one_month_reasoning: No Snowflake earnings in the window: Q2 FY27 was reported 2026-09-02 and Q3 FY27 (quarter ending Oct 31) is normally reported late Nov/early Dec, after 2026-10-30. Events inside the window are indirect: hyperscaler Q3 prints (Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon in late October), which set the tone for consumption/data-infrastructure names, and settlement/hedging flows around the just-announced $3.5B zero-coupon convertible (convert-arb short hedging typically weighs for days after pricing, largely already reflected in the ~4% drop on 2026-09-28). Post-earnings drift after a big beat-and-raise is a mild positive; the sector-wide software selloff and the fall from the $384.56 high is a mild negative. Net: essentially neutral, lognormal centred on ~$337.5 with a slight downward tilt, monthly vol ~17.5% (62%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM revenue (Sep-2027 NTM revenue ~$9.6B x 14x, 50%), EV/NTM adjusted FCF (~$2.4B x 45x, 25%) and P/E on FY29 non-GAAP EPS (~$4.50 x 75x, 25%), with ~$3B net cash and ~390M diluted shares, giving ~$331 per share one year out.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 ~$9.6B x 14x EV/NTM = $134B EV + $3B net cash = $137B / 390M shares

inputs_detail.input: Q2 FY27 total revenue / product revenue

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 total revenue ~$6.3B (product guide $6.07B plus ~4% services); FY28 +30% to ~$8.2B (decel from 36-38% guided Q3 growth, RPO +30% supports ~30%); FY29 +26% to ~$10.3B; NTM Oct-27..Sep-28 blends ~2/3 FY29 and ~1/3 late FY28 run-rate. Peer checks: MongoDB Atlas steady ~29% and raised, hyperscalers accelerating (AWS +37%, Azure +43%, GCP +82%) imply the consumption backdrop supports ~30% near term.

High-growth SaaS (25-40% growth, NRR>120%) trades 8-15x NTM per public-multiples trackers, which listed SNOW ~13x and Datadog ~12x; SNOW currently implies ~17x on my NTM ~$7.3B. By Sep-2027 growth decelerates toward mid/high-20s, so I assume partial compression toward the top of the peer band (14x), keeping a premium for 126% NRR and AI-driven acceleration.

Jul-31-2026 cash+ST+LT investments $4.33B less $2.28B converts = ~$2.0B; new $3.5B zero-coupon converts are roughly cash-neutral to net debt at issue (proceeds offset debt, partly used for capped calls/repurchasing old notes); add ~$1.3B of FCF over the year less buybacks/capped call cost -> ~$3B.
Q3 FY27 guide 382M non-GAAP diluted plus ~2% net SBC dilution and some convert dilution above capped-call ceilings, partly offset by buybacks.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM adjusted FCF at Sep-2027 ~$2.4B x 45x = $108B + $3B net cash = $111B / 390M

inputs_detail.derivation: ~24-25% margin (modest expansion from 23% guide as operating margin guide rises 13.5%->14.5%) on ~$9.6B NTM revenue.
Adjusted FCF excludes heavy SBC; a 45x multiple (~2.2% yield) is consistent with the 13-15x EV/sales band at ~25% margin for a ~25%+ grower.
FY29 revenue ~$10.3B x ~19% non-GAAP operating margin (from 14.5% FY27 guide, +~2pts/yr) = ~$1.95B, plus interest income, ~20% tax -> ~$1.75B / 390M shares.
Consistent with ~14x EV/sales at ~19% operating margin; high-growth software on early-stage margins trades on sales rather than earnings, so this is a cross-check.

bear.story: AI consumption step-up proves lumpy, Databricks (80% growth, $6.9B run-rate, free-tier bundling of Lakebase/Agent Bricks) and open Iceberg formats take new workloads, growth decelerates to low 20s by FY28 and multiple compresses to ~8-9x NTM sales amid a software de-rating.

base.story: Growth glides from 37% to high-20s, NRR stays ~120s, margins expand ~2pts/yr; multiple compresses from ~17x to ~14x NTM sales, offset by ~30% revenue growth, leaving the stock modestly above today.

bull.story: CoCo/CoWork AI products keep driving consolidation onto Snowflake; growth holds 33%+ through FY28, hyperscaler acceleration keeps consumption strong, and the market keeps a 17-18x multiple on ~$10B NTM revenue.

thesis_break_reason: ~36% below today and below the pre-Q2 trading range; at ~$215 the market would be pricing growth falling into the low 20s or an AI/Databricks share-loss story (NRR sliding toward 115%) rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise. A guide-down in product revenue or a sharp drop in $1M+ customer adds would confirm it.

reasoning: Industry lane. The value chain is uniformly strong: hyperscalers accelerated in Q2 2026 (AWS +37%, Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82% with $514B backlog), MongoDB Atlas grew ~29% for a fifth straight quarter with healthy consumption and a raised guide, and Databricks' run-rate hit $6.9B (+80%), with AI products ~25% of ARR. That confirms strong data/AI infrastructure demand but also that Databricks is growing more than twice as fast as Snowflake and has passed it in run-rate (the gap widened from $0.49B to $1.6B between March and June 2026), a share-shift risk. Spend data (Ramp, Sep-2026) still shows Snowflake as the most-adopted warehouse (64%) and the one winning the most switchers, with Databricks growing adoption faster. Snowflake's own Q2 FY27 (product +37%, NRR 126%, RPO +30%, FY guide raised to $6.07B/+36%, op margin 14.5%) and post-print target raises to $424-470 show the momentum, but the stock already trades at ~17x NTM sales against a 8-15x high-growth peer band. My blended fair value one year out is ~$331 (EV/sales $352, FCF $285, P/E $337): revenue growth of ~30% roughly offsets expected multiple compression. Scenarios $190/$355/$530 at 25/50/25 give a mean ~$358; I set a lognormal-like distribution with median ~$345 and sigma ~0.52 (slightly below 62% realized vol since the last year included a large re-rating) with a slightly fatter left tail for the competitive and de-rating risk. Research was focused (about 12 queries/fetches); CNBC blocked fetching, so Databricks figures rely on the Tunguz post and search summaries.
